messages:
elaine: Heads-up — I can see traces for the redirect flow in the Console but the app logs don't include the same trace_id. Sentry shows the error span, but grepping pod logs for that trace id returns nothing.

mike: ack. which log path? k8s stdout/json -> fluentd -> datadog or the datadog-forwarder path?

elaine: stdout -> fluentd -> datadog. We use python-json-logger to stringify logs. My hunch is our middleware is not capturing the W3C traceparent header.

jordan: we ran into related issues before — async tasks drop context if it isn't propagated to the LoggingContext. Are we using otel-instrumentation for the web tier?

sam: service = FastAPI + Uvicorn + Starlette middleware. We have otel tracer for spans, but we never wired the log correlation integration.

mike: quick implementation idea: add a logging Filter that pulls the current span trace id and injects into the log record. Example (py):
```python
from opentelemetry.trace import get_current_span

def trace_filter(record):
    span = get_current_span()
    if span is not None and span.get_span_context().is_valid:
        record.trace_id = format(span.get_span_context().trace_id, '032x')
    else:
        record.trace_id = None
    return True
```
Add this filter to our logger config (structlog or stdlib).

elaine: that should work. two design q's: 1) field name — "trace_id" vs "traceId" vs "trace.trace_id"? 2) format — keep hex string or integer? datadog sometimes expects numeric.

jordan: I'd standardize on snake_case "trace_id" in logs (32-char hex). We can also emit an integer field trace_id_int if downstream wants that. Keep otel span attributes as usual (trace.id etc.).

sam: also note sampling mismatch: if traces are sampled low, you might have logs with trace_id but no trace in backend. that's expected. correlation still helps for the sampled traces.

mike: ops budget note: adding trace_id to every line increases payload and might create facets if team makes it indexed in Datadog. Finance ping?

devex: small UX idea — Console Logs view should show "Open trace" next to a log when trace_id present. Link -> /console/traces?trace_id=<id>. We can gate behind feature flag.

elaine: rollout suggestion:
- add log filter middleware in service lib with unit tests
- feature flag LOG_TRACE_INJECTION (default off)
- smoke canary in staging, then 10% prod pods in eu-west-1
- run datadog ingestion checks and alert if index growth > X%

jordan: I'll add the canary rollout stanza to the kustomize/rollouts YAML and wire the flag to the configmap.

mike: I'll build the python filter + a node variant for other services. include unit + an integration test talking to our smoke harness. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sam: for observability tests: generate an instrumented trace, emit a log inside the span, assert datadog receives a log with trace_id and that Console trace lookup resolves. I can add that to the smoke test suite.

infra-bot: CI: build #3789 queued for mike's branch -> running unit tests :gear: (see https://ci.redwood-inference/builds/3789)

elaine: tiny convention note: let's standardize on 32-char lowercase hex for trace_id in logs, and optionally include trace_id_int when requested. Keep both behind the flag.

mike: +1, will include both fields and flag. Also add a concise doc blurb in our observability README.

devex: :thumbsup: I'll mock the Console "Open trace" and add to the product review board.

mike: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/services/pull/642 — feel free to review.

sam: left a couple of comments on the PR.

infra-bot: deployment to staging complete for canary service (2 pods) — logs show trace_id for test flows.

elaine: verified E2E on staging: logs have trace_id and Console "Open trace" resolves correctly. Will start prod canary tomorrow morning. If anyone sees mismatches before then, ping me.

mike: noted, will keep an eye on ingest and facet creation.

elaine: thanks all, creating the ticket and will link this thread.
